title: Level 3 stores the references only the toolchain sees, and a roster of the targets it defines
objective: Level 3 also keeps the references only the language's toolchain sees, for definitions inside the project: uses of the project's own fields, consts and statics, its types and variants in patterns, and its functions passed as values, so that `intent search --target` answers who uses one of them exactly and a never-referenced answer is exact for those kinds; and it keeps a roster of the targets the toolchain defines, so `--target` tells a target nothing references from a misspelt one.
context:
Ruled by hv on 2026-09-17 ("Ok, A now, then B post."; hv decision 22 on hv's board) after ST0076 landed level 3 under rule A: a resolved row always joins a written reference (same file, line and name), and a reference only the toolchain sees is counted and not stored (vc decision 25 (2), the level-3 core's module doc). This thread is B, for the line after the close-out.

Measured on the Intent repository by vc on 2026-09-17, on the live `intent index resolve --lang rust` run (ea81a6c58, store schema 29) and recounted independently from the export and the store to the unit: rust-analyzer reports 242,375 references; 133,788 are stored under rule A; 74,354 are dropped by design (57,482 locals, 16,845 operator references, 27 multi-line); 34,233 are real references the syntax index never wrote, counted as unmatched and not stored. Of those, 12,859 are uses of the project's own fields, consts and statics; 6,051 are mentions of its own modules (`mod x;` lines and path heads); 1,484 are its own types and variants where the syntax queries do not look, mostly patterns; 190 are its own functions passed as values, plus 2 macros; and 13,647 point outside the project (`std` path segments, `#[test]` and derive names, `Ok`, `Err`, `Some` and `None`), which nobody asks about. So the population this thread stores is about 20,600 rows here, some 16% more than rule A stores, and it is Rust-only in effect: the Elixir tracer reports no field access.

What it needs, as vc sized it (M to L): one predicate at write in the level-3 core (`intentsvcs::index::resolved::join`), which today drops a reference that joins no written row; a hit shape in the search surfaces for a reference that has no syntax row (a level-3-only reference carries its path, line and name from the toolchain and no `symbols` row); a table of the targets the toolchain defines, one schema rung, filled by the Rust reader from the export's definition occurrences and by the Elixir reader from the definition rows it prints; `--target` on a defined target no row references answering "defined at path:line, referenced by nothing" instead of the note that a target nothing references and a misspelt one read the same; `intent index status` counting stored-unwritten rows apart from the external unmatched; and arms for each. The side table has no foreign key to the written rows, so nothing landed under rule A is undone.
